fields.description:
`docs/adr/` holds 83 files but only 61 distinct numbers. 17 numbers are reused — including FIVE
unrelated ADRs numbered 0037, all `Status: Accepted`, all flat in one directory. There is no index.
Meanwhile `AGENTS.md:42` cites "ADR 0025" by bare number and `CONTRIBUTING.md:173` sanctions bare
ADR references in commit trailers.

Design work established the cause and the safe remediation:

**Cause.** Every collision landed within ~3 hours median. But only 6 of 22 were true in-flight
Gerrit races; 16 of 22 were stale-base — the earlier ADR had already landed and the author never
refetched. A pre-merge check would have caught 16 of 22.

**Prevention is git's, not CI's.** A pre-merge uniqueness check on a monotonic counter is racy by
construction, and ADR 0047 explicitly accepts that a change may land without re-running CI after a
server-side rebase. The race-free mechanism is a per-number marker file `docs/adr/.numbers/NNNN`
whose content is the ADR's filename: two ADRs claiming one number produce an add/add conflict,
which Rebase-If-Necessary cannot auto-resolve. Empirically tested in throwaway repos: conflict iff
same number, ZERO false conflicts. A shared sorted index was tested and rejected — it conflicts on
EVERY concurrent addition (~23% of this repo's ADR additions would conflict spuriously), and a
contributor would resolve it by regenerating, silently producing an index containing both.

**Renumbering is approved** (limited user base). Earliest-landed keeps the number; 22 files move to
numbers above 0061. Historical disambiguation: ancestry alone resolves 23 of 90 commit references,
co-landing 40, topic-matching 86 — 4 remain ambiguous and only 1 resists human resolution.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `docs/adr/.numbers/NNNN` marker files exist for every ADR, content = the ADR filename
- [x] CI asserts the bijection between ADRs and markers, and that no two markers share content
- [x] A generated `docs/adr/README.md` index exists, grouped by workstream, showing full slugs
- [x] `docs/adr/RENUMBERING.md` records the old-to-new mapping and the per-reference resolution table, with tiers marked and the unresolvable reference recorded as UNRESOLVED
- [x] The 17 duplicate numbers are resolved, earliest-landed keeping the number
- [x] Moved ADRs carry a "previously numbered" header; kept ADRs carry an ambiguity-window note
- [x] `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md:602`'s ADR range citation is replaced by an explicit list
## CURRENT-STATE CORRECTION (the header figures are stale; superseded here)

The description's "83 files / 61 distinct numbers / above 0061" reflects the board at ticket-creation
time. As of this implementation the ADR corpus grew (the sibling comment-triage shards 9ce8/4b94/ad16/ab77
landed NEW ADRs 0062-0069). Authoritative current state, re-measured from the tree:

- **91 ADR files**, 69 distinct numbers, **17 duplicate numbers** (5x0037; 3x0007, 3x0035; and 0008-0012,
  0015, 0016, 0026, 0031, 0032, 0036, 0038, 0040, 0041 doubled) = **22 files to move**.
- **Moved ADRs are renumbered to 0070-0091** (NOT "above 0061" — 0062-0069 are now taken by the landed
  sibling ADRs). Target range chosen to sit strictly above the highest existing number (0069).
- Tiebreak unchanged: **earliest-landed keeps its number**; the 22 movers are assigned 0070..0091 in
  ascending landing-date order (full git history, not the shallow-clone graft point). The exact old->new
  map is recorded in docs/adr/RENUMBERING.md and is the authoritative artifact for AC "resolve the 17
  duplicate numbers".

All seven acceptance criteria stand as written; only the numeric targets (file count, and the 0070-0091
destination band) are corrected here.

## Cross-reference handling — stale-reference remediation (addresses plan-review T7/E6)

Renumbering strands references. A reference to a MOVED ADR's old number now resolves to the KEPT ADR
of that collision group (wrong target); a reference that always meant the kept ADR stays correct.
This is handled explicitly, not left to chance:

**Sweep + resolve.** Every `ADR NNNN` / `adr/NNNN-slug` reference in `docs/` and `src/` (outside
`docs/adr/` file bodies) that names a collision number is resolved to the SPECIFIC ADR it means (by
adjacent slug when present, else by topic/context), and rewritten to that ADR's FINAL number. The
per-reference resolution and its tier (slug-exact / topic-matched / ancestry / UNRESOLVED) is the
resolution table already required by AC "RENUMBERING.md".

**Worked example.** `docs/architecture.md` mentions "the transport retry policy (ADR 0037)". The
0037 group keeps `0037-oss-contribution-intake-posture` (earliest-landed) and moves
`0037-transport-retry` -> **0087**. The slug "transport retry" disambiguates: this reference meant
the moved ADR, so it is rewritten to `ADR 0087`. A bare "ADR 0037" whose context is OSS-intake stays
`0037` (it now correctly names the sole surviving 0037).

**Proving command (new AC below).** A referential-integrity assertion in the same CI check
(`scripts/check_adr_numbers.py`) fails when any `adr/NNNN-slug` link in `docs/` points to a filename
that does not exist, or any `docs/adr/*.md` body cross-links a slug/number with no matching file.
This turns "no stranded reference" into an enforced, reproducible check rather than a claim. (Bare
prose "ADR NNNN" with no slug is advisory-only — it cannot be mechanically bound to one ADR — and any
residue is recorded UNRESOLVED in RENUMBERING.md.)

## Acceptance Criteria (addendum — supersedes nothing, adds the T7/E6 proving path)

- [x] No stranded ADR cross-reference remains: every `adr/NNNN-slug` link in `docs/` (and every
      slug/number cross-link inside `docs/adr/*.md`) resolves to an existing, unique ADR file, and
      references that named a MOVED ADR are rewritten to its new 0070-0091 number. `scripts/check_adr_numbers.py`
      asserts this referential integrity (proving command: the check exits non-zero on a dangling
      `adr/*-slug` link), and RENUMBERING.md records each rewritten reference with its resolution tier.
